steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Cream brown and white sugars with butter in a medium bowl. Stir in vanilla, egg white, and water. Sift together flour, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl; stir into creamed mixture. Mix in chocolate chips.
Drop dough by heaping spoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly browned and edges are set, 8 to 10 minutes. Allow cookies to cool on baking sheets for 10 minutes before transferring them to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Light Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This is a tasty recipe for soft and chewy low-fat chocolate chip cookies. Don't try to double it; it doesn't turn out.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was a great one for simple, yet delicious cookies! I did make a few changes though. Since I didn't have any semi-sweet chocolate chips, I used milk chocolate chips instead. I also used 3 tbsps of HOT water. To top it off, I chilled the dough in the fridge for 30 minutes. Boy, was I glad I did all of this! The cookies turned out great with the changes and not flat at all unlike some people's reviews. I suggest that you bake it for at least 10 minutes if you want nice and chewy, almost cake-like cookies. If you like your cookies more on the "rough" side than I suggest you bake it for 12 minutes. Hope my review helps you out!

Best light version I've found so far! They really gave me that chocolate chip cookie taste without all the fat and calories. After reading some of the comments from others, I decided to make the following changes to this recipe:

I used 3 TBSP butter and 3 TBSP no sugar added apple sauce, reducing the water to only 1 TBSP. I also used a bit less brown sugar (half a cup) and they still came out plenty sweet. For the flour, I used one cup all purpose and half cup spelt flour, and I did increase the baking soda to 1 tsp to help keep them from flattening. I also used mini chocolate chips instead of regular and refrigerated the dough before baking. They held their shape nicely while baking. After about 12 minutes in the oven, they came out perfect! I was really quite pleased with the result.

With the above changes, these are 90 calories per cookie, with 1.7g saturated fat and 9.3g of sugar. A nice compromise for those trying to manage their weight. I was able to eat two of them with no guilt. I'll definitely be making these again. :)
I used 4 Tblsp butter and 2 Tblsp applesauce instead of 6 Tblsp margarine or butter, and they turned out well.
I used 1 cup of flour and 1/2 cup of whole wheat. I also added 2tbls of flax seed.They turned out awsome, kids ate them up!! just dont over bake...
Changed 1/2 cup of mixed sugars for three tbs of honey, added orange zest, cacao and a pinch cinnamon and nutmeg.

I double the recipe every time, and they turn out great! I use one whole egg rather than two whites, otherwise I just double everything as written. My family doesn’t notice that they are lighter than the usual cookies.
I used whole wheat flour and used canola oil instead of butter . I baked it for 10 minutes after reading the reviews. The dough was crumbly but otherwise, the recipe is great!
Great recipe! I did change it up a bit by cutting it to 4 tbsps of butter...I also added 1/3 cup rolled oatmeal. They turned out chewy with a bit of crunch. Will definitely make them again!
This came out good. I used 3/4 cup coconut oil instead of the butter and I used 1 cup of whole wheat flour and 1/2 cup all purpose flour and 1 tsp of vanilla.

i'm impressed with this recipe. I substituted all purpose flour with brown rice flour, and I used 3 tbsp of butter and 3 tbsp of apple sauce instead of 6 tbsp of butter. I added 1/2 c coconut flakes because I love the chocolate/coconut combo. They came out light and moist and delicious. I'll use this recipe again.

I was really pleased with how these cookies turned out. I substituted Splenda for the 1/4 cup of white sugar. Instead of the 6 TBS butter, I used 2 TBS light butter, 3 TBS unsweetened applesauce, and 1 TBS margarine (an odd mix, I know; I was using what I had on hand). I used 1 cup of white flour and 1/2 cup of wheat flour. Finally, as another reviewer suggested, I made sure the water I added was HOT water. I did chill the dough for a short time and baked the cookies for 10 minutes. They came out brown and the flavor was great; however, they are cake-like. I am so pleased that this yolk-free recipe tastes so good and my husband had to ask what was different to make them light.
I really loved this recipe! It's still a bit sweet for my taste,but it's still delicious. I used the hot water and I baked them for 8 minutes.
I found that they did not have much flavour besides the chocolate chips. Maybe add some extra vanilla? Otherwise, they turned out perfect! Soft and moist.
